node.title: Append-only admin audit log with 7-year retention
node.description: Every admin action must be written to an append-only audit log that keeps entries for 7 years.

provenance.quote: Every admin action must be written to an append-only audit log that keeps entries for 7 years.

ambiguities.question: What counts as an 'admin action'? Which roles, and which operations (reads, config changes, user management, logins)?
What must each audit entry contain (actor, timestamp, target, action, before/after values, source IP, outcome)?
How is 'append-only' to be enforced and verified (storage-level immutability, WORM storage, hash chaining, DB permissions), and does it need to resist tampering by admins themselves?
What happens to entries after 7 years: must they be deleted, may they be deleted, or may they be retained longer? Does the 7 years run from entry creation?
What should happen if writing the audit entry fails: block the admin action (fail closed) or allow it and alert?
Who may read or export the audit log, and must access to it be controlled or itself logged?
Which existing system, services, or storage should host the log, and what regulatory or compliance regime (if any) drives the 7-year requirement?

acceptance_criteria.statement: Every admin action is written to an audit log.
The audit log is append-only: existing entries cannot be modified or deleted.
Audit log entries are kept for 7 years.

revisions.summary: Initial translation of human request into Intent IR v1
